anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer persistently chooses sub-optimal execution plans even though statistics are valid, leading to excessive resource demand per statement.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly: Standby or downstream replicas fall behind because they cannot receive, write, or apply WAL/redo as fast as the primary generates it.
CPU Resource Anomaly: Database processes saturate host CPU, starving other activities and lengthening scheduling latency.

When these three root causes coincide, the sub-optimal plans inflate CPU consumption on the primary and, once shipped, on every replica that must re-execute the same inefficient SQL during logical or physical apply. The resulting CPU saturation slows local query execution, background housekeeping, and the replica apply threads simultaneously. In parallel, the replication channel begins to lag; monitoring views show rapidly widening LSN/SCN gaps, growing retained logs, and increasing replica staleness. On both primary and replicas, users observe longer query latencies, stalled failover readiness, and escalating disk usage as log recycling is blocked by outstanding replication positions.

Causally, poor plan selection is the ignition point: inflated row loops, missing pruning, or mis-estimated joins drive CPU and generate larger transaction logs. The surge in CPU demand pushes the host to saturation, lengthening process run-queue times and slowing the single-threaded or lightly parallelized apply workers on replicas. As apply throughput falls behind the primary’s heightened log generation rate, replication lag compounds, which in turn prevents log truncation and keeps more redo on disk, increasing I/O pressure. The feedback loop—sub-optimal plans → CPU exhaustion → slower apply → larger backlogs—propagates across all nodes, making each individual anomaly harder to diagnose in isolation and severely degrading overall database performance and resilience.

entry.official_description: Transaction isolation level (tx_isolation) is set to SERIALIZABLE, which is not compatible with Group Replication
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
